propositions: Phase 3 remediation proposers reach Phase 4 approval without validation that proposed remediations are justified by reachable harm or do not reverse recorded decisions
Identical evidence consumed by two blind proposers measures prompt stability rather than correctness, creating a false confidence signal in convergence
No mechanism exists to classify findings where harm is plausible but unreachable, forcing their remediation moves to approval unflagged
The five-phase pipeline lacks a systematic check for whether a proposed change reverses a deliberate, documented project decision and whether the evidence basis has changed
Phase 2 verification scores finding validity but does not validate that the proposed remediation direction addresses reachable harm or acknowledges prior decisions
Phase 4 approval lacks surfaced record of prior decisions, evidence changes, or hardening-vs-defect classification needed to assess remediation soundness
